title.en: Eleven million dollars and a front door

dek.en: 1kx leads an $11M seed round, the Discord opens to the public, and Optimum starts explaining itself as the memory layer the world computer forgot.

en: April was the month Optimum stopped being a name on a slide. In one week it announced an $11 million seed round, opened its Discord, put up its website and documentation, and held its biggest X Space yet.

The pitch was still broad: decentralized memory for any chain, with Optimum P2P as the first product. Validators and Ethereum would come into focus later. For now the message was that blockchains are computers missing their RAM.
On 15 April Optimum announced an $11 million seed round led by 1kx, with CMT Digital, Finality Capital, Robot Ventures, GSR, Chorus One and others.
The Discord opened to the public on 14 April. Optimum said a week later it had more than 100,000 members, and called its first community call for 2 May.
Muriel Médard wrote in CoinDesk that Web3 has a memory problem, and she and Kent Lin went back to the Harvard Blockchain Conference, where Optimum started a year earlier.

body.en: On 15 April Optimum announced an $11 million seed round led by 1kx, to build what it called the first high performance memory infrastructure for any blockchain. CoinDesk, Blockworks and The Defiant covered it the same day. Backers posting their support included CMT Digital, Finality Capital, GSR, Chorus One, CMS Holdings, Caladan, SNZ, MH Ventures and Triton, and CMT published its investment thesis on the networking layer a day later. Optimum also put out its first blog post and a five minute introduction video.

The invite link went up on 14 April with a warning that it would expire in three hours. In its weekly recap on 19 April Optimum listed the seed round, the Discord launch, a new website with documentation and its largest X Space, and said the server already had more than 100,000 members. That figure is Optimum’s own and counts joins, not active members. On 28 April it called the first community call for 2 May in the Discord, open to holders of the OG role.

sources: Optimum on X, first community call

body.en: On 1 April CoinDesk published an opinion piece by Muriel Médard arguing that Web3 lacks a real memory layer: gossip protocols, full replication and mempools are best effort patches, not a design. Optimum followed with a thread comparing today’s data handling to a pile of laundry next to a tidy closet, and described Optimum P2P as a memory bus and deRAM as decentralized memory built on random linear network coding.

A thread on 1 April explained random linear network coding as turning data into a math puzzle before sending it: the sender mixes packets with random equations, nodes along the way remix them, and the receiver solves the puzzle once it has collected enough pieces. The thread said independent Ethereum Foundation research had shown proof of concept gains of up to 20 times in bandwidth with RLNC. On 21 April Médard explained the idea in under five minutes on video, and on 30 April the blog published Battle of the Codes, comparing RLNC with Reed Solomon and fountain codes.

sources: Optimum on X, five minute video
Optimum blog, Battle of the Codes

body.en: Optimum traced its origins to the Harvard Blockchain Conference a year earlier, and on 26 April both co-founders were back on its programme. Kent Lin sat on a decentralized infrastructure panel and Médard presented on Web3’s memory problem, describing a blockchain as a computer that lacks a memory unit and a bus. Optimum also announced that Médard would speak at Consensus in Toronto on 16 May.

title.en: Spaces with investors and a validator

body.en: Two more X Spaces filled the month. On 17 April Wei Dai of 1kx joined the co-founders to talk about why chains need memory infrastructure; a community member wrote up a summary on Mirror. On 24 April Aryon of CMT Digital and Masha of Everstake gave an investor’s and a validator’s view in Making Blockchains Feel Fast Again. Everstake would later become one of the first testnet partners.

title.en: From the Discord: the OG role

body.en: The first thing the new server handed out was a role. On 16 April Optimum reopened claims for the OG role through a Galxe quest, explaining that its first attempt had drawn so much traffic it crashed the Discord API. The OG role marked early members and was meant to unlock perks later. The claim window closed on 23 April, when the Optimum Kickoff Quest ended. The same week the Optimum Goggles meme contest asked members to put the goggle logo on anything, from friends to pets, with winners to be named on the first community call.
